steps: Facing the house, look left of the front windows — the gate is just left of the front door.
The gate keypad is on its right. Press the large bottom button to wake it, enter the code, then the checkmark.
Walk down the alley (it's lit — if the lights are out, let Keith know!) to the shared courtyard.
At the cottage door keypad, press unlock (lower left) to wake it, then enter the same code.
When leaving, close the door and press the right lock button — and please re-lock the gate the same way.

howToRide.intro: Bay Area transit looks like alphabet soup from the outside. It isn't — here's the whole thing on one page.

payment.name: Clipper in Apple or Google Pay
payment.detail: What Keith would do. Add it once in Wallet, then hold your phone to the reader. Works on Muni, BART, Caltrain and every regional bus, and it gives you free transfers.

payment.name: Contactless bank card
payment.detail: Tap your own card on Muni and BART. Simple, but no transfer credit.

payment.name: Physical Clipper card
payment.detail: From the machines at Balboa Park BART if you'd rather not use a phone.

payment.name: Kids ride free
payment.detail: Under 10 walks on with you on Muni — no tag, no fare. Youth up to 18 ride Muni free too, with a youth Clipper.

muni.detail: Buses, trolleybuses, the Metro trains (J K L M N T) and the cable cars. One flat fare, ~$2.85, and it buys you 120 minutes of unlimited transfers if you tap with Clipper. Board at any door on the Metro; tap on entry on buses.
muni.note: K stops 2 min from the gate

bart.detail: Regional trains to Oakland, Berkeley and SFO. Distance-based fare, so you tap in and out at the gates. Balboa Park is our station, 9 minutes on foot, and SFO is a straight ride.

caltrain.detail: Electric trains to Palo Alto, Mountain View and San José from 4th & King. Tap in and out like BART. Take the K or T to get there. Worth it if you're heading to the South Bay for a day.

regionalBus.detail:
AC Transit — Oakland, Berkeley, the East Bay
Golden Gate Transit & Ferry — Marin, Sausalito, Larkspur
SamTrans — San Mateo County and the coast
All of them take the same Clipper in your Wallet.

howToRide.tip: Two habits that make this easy: check departures before you walk out (Google Maps isn't reliable for Muni — use the Transit app or 511.org), and always tap off on BART and Caltrain.

byPlane.name: San Francisco (SFO)
byPlane.summary: The easiest airport by far. BART runs from the terminal straight to Balboa Park, a short walk from the cottage.
byPlane.transit: Follow signs for BART (it's in the International Terminal — take AirTrain if you land at a domestic terminal). Any San Francisco-bound train stops at Balboa Park, about 30 minutes. From there it's an 8-minute walk, or one stop on the K toward City College. Add a Clipper card to Apple/Google Pay and just tap — no ticket machine needed.
byPlane.rentalCar: Take AirTrain Blue Line to the Rental Car Center. From the airport it's I-380 W to I-280 N, exit Ocean Ave — about 20 minutes without traffic.
byPlane.rideshare: Uber/Lyft pick up on level 5 of the domestic garage (follow the signs from baggage claim). Roughly $30–45 and 20–25 minutes to the cottage.

byPlane.name: Oakland (OAK)
byPlane.sub: Across the bay — about an hour by BART
byPlane.summary: Often the cheapest Southwest flights. BART gets you here without a car.
byPlane.transit: Take the BART Airport Connector tram to Coliseum station, then a San Francisco-bound train. Daly City trains stop at Balboa Park directly; otherwise change at 19th St Oakland. About an hour total, then the 8-minute walk.
byPlane.rentalCar: Rental shuttle from outside baggage claim. Drive I-880 N over the Bay Bridge, then US-101 S to I-280 S, exit Ocean Ave — 45 minutes to an hour depending on bridge traffic.
byPlane.rideshare: Pickup is on the curb outside arrivals. Expect $60–80 and 35–50 minutes depending on bridge traffic.

byPlane.name: San Jose (SJC)
byPlane.sub: South Bay — plan on a car or a long transit ride
byPlane.summary: About 45 miles south. Fine if the fare is right, but budget real travel time.
byPlane.transit: It's a trek: the free VTA 60 bus to Santa Clara Caltrain, Caltrain north to San Francisco, then Muni to the cottage — about 2 to 2.5 hours. Doable, but a car is much faster from here.
byPlane.rentalCar: Rental cars are a shuttle ride from the terminals. Drive US-101 N or I-280 N (prettier) to the Ocean Ave exit — about 50 minutes without traffic.
byPlane.rideshare: Pickup zones are outside each terminal. Expect $80–110 and about an hour.

byPlane.name: Santa Rosa (STS)
byPlane.summary: Tiny wine-country airport about 60 miles north. Honestly, rent a car.
byPlane.transit: Possible but slow: SMART train from the airport area to Larkspur, Golden Gate Ferry to the Embarcadero, then Muni — close to 3 hours, though the ferry ride is gorgeous.
byPlane.rentalCar: Rental counters are right in the small terminal. US-101 S across the Golden Gate Bridge, then I-280 S to Ocean Ave — about 1.5 hours outside rush hour.
byPlane.rideshare: Availability up there is thin and it's a long ride — $120+ when you can get one. A rental is almost always the better call.

arrive.driving: From either direction on I-280, take the Ocean Ave exit and head west — the cottage is a few blocks up on Harold Ave, just off Ocean. Your parking spot is the paved space directly in front of the house, between the sidewalk and the front windows (details under Parking). The cottage is down a narrow alley left of the front windows.
arrive.publicTransit: You don't need a car here. BART (Balboa Park, 9-minute walk) covers the region and runs direct to SFO; the K Ingleside streetcar (2-minute walk on Ocean Ave) runs downtown; buses 29, 8, 49, 43 and 54 are all within a couple of blocks. Add Clipper to Apple or Google Pay and tap on — no ticket needed. Full lines, stops and live departures are in Around Here.

parking.main: This is the parking spot — it's slightly angled from the curb. Please pull up as close to the wall (in front of the two windows) as possible so the back of the car doesn't block too much of the sidewalk. Leave room on the left for the gate and walkway, and get close to the plant on the right. Let me know if you have any questions!
parking.limit: There's room for one car under 17 ft — most sedans and SUVs fit fine.
parking.street: You can also park on the street. It's 2-hour parking Mon–Fri 8am–5pm, so a car parked overnight is fine until 10am, and anything parked after 3pm is clear for the evening. Street cleaning is the 1st and 3rd Monday on the cottage side of Harold, and the 1st and 3rd Thursday across the street — double-check the curb signs.

secondCar.intro: Need a second spot? Here are 3 places that usually have open street parking:
spots: The other side of the gas station has a few spots behind the bus stop — no 2-hour limit and no street cleaning.
Frida Kahlo Way has no 2-hour limit, but street cleaning runs Tue/Thu 12am–6am — park after 6am, or on Mon/Wed/Fri, and you're fine.
Geneva Ave is 2-hour parking only (so you'd need to move between 10am and 4pm), with street cleaning Fridays 7–8am.
secondCar.outro: There's more parking a little farther out with no 2-hour limit. The SpotAngels app is great for finding it — or just ask Keith.
